subject: MAP: CardioAI POC environment — org setup, API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cardioai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: MAP: CardioAI POC environment — org setup, API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the conversation yesterday. As discussed, attaching an updated mutual action plan (MAP) that captures the POC activation path and responsibilities. Key items we need to lock in this week so the POC can start the week of Nov 15: 

- Org & admin access: confirm two CardioAI org admins (email addresses) so we can provision production-like org-scoped API keys.
- API keys: Redwood will generate ephemeral API keys for the POC; we need confirmed admin emails for provisioning and one rotation contact.
- IP allowlist: provide the source IPs/subnets you will add to allowlist (we list Redwood public egress below).
- VPC peering: preferred CIDR for peering and an initial /16 or /20 — we can peer from our staging VPC.

Proposed timeline (high-level):
- Nov 5: confirm admins + network owners
- Nov 6–9: exchange PE/technical info (firewall rules, routes)
- Nov 10–12: schedule peering window and test connectivity
- Nov 15: POC kickoff, run initial inference tests

Attachments: CardioAI_MAP_v2.pdf (MAP with milestones + acceptance criteria)

Ask: Can you confirm the org admin emails and the network contact (for VPC peering) today? If Procurement needs an SOW/PO, loop them in and we’ll provide the finance packet.

Thanks —

Grace O'Connor
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: CardioAI_MAP_v2.pdf (application/pdf))

From: Samir Patel <samir@cardioai.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cardioai.net>, procurement@cardioai.com
Date: 2026-11-05T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: CardioAI POC environment — org setup, API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering

Grace —

Appreciate the clear plan. Quick answers from our side: 

- Org admins: samir@cardioai.com and linda.morris@cardioai.com (both ok to receive provisioning emails).
- Network contact: Alex Chen (cc'd) is our network lead and will coordinate the peer.
- VPC CIDR: we prefer 10.40.0.0/16 for the POC VPC. If you need a smaller block for routing, we can adjust to /20.
- Allowlist: we'll allow specific Redwood egress IPs but prefer to receive the full set in CSV.

Two questions from Alex (copied):
1) Will the peering be auto-provisioned from your side or do we need to create a peering request?
2) How are the ephemeral API keys rotated during the POC — daily or on-demand?

Procurement — could you confirm if you need a formal SOW or a simple PO for the reserved trial capacity?

Thanks,
Samir
CEO, CardioAI

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cardioai.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cardioai.net>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T13:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: CardioAI POC environment — org setup, API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering

Samir / Alex —

Quick technical notes to address Alex's questions and unblock network setup: 

1) Peering flow: Redwood can initiate the peering from our console once CardioAI creates the peering request on your cloud account. Typical steps: CardioAI creates peering, shares the peering id, Redwood accepts and we advertise routes. If you prefer, we can provide IaC snippets to create the peering.

2) Ephemeral API keys: For the POC we will issue keys that are valid for 7 days by default and allow on-demand rotation via the console or API. If you want daily rotation, we can set that up — it will require the client to re-fetch keys via the admin email flow.

3) Allowlist CSV: attaching the current Redwood egress list (network_allowlist.csv) — please add these IPs to your firewall and return a test rule confirmation. We also recommend a single /32 for the peering VPN endpoint if you plan to lock down management ports.

Proposed peering windows (PST): Nov 11 02:00–04:00 OR Nov 12 22:00–00:00 — pick the one that fits your ops. We'll reserve the slot after you confirm.

Next steps checklist:
- Alex: create peering request or tell us preferred IaC approach
- Samir: confirm admins (got them) and procurement needs
- Grace/Neha: share SOW/finance packet if procurement requests it

(Attachment: network_allowlist.csv (text/csv))

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cardioai.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@cardioai.net>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: CardioAI POC environment — org setup, API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering

Samir / Alex —

Thanks for the fast responses. Confirming the plan from Redwood's side: 

- Org admins: samir@cardioai.com and linda.morris@cardioai.com added to the provisioning list; we’ll send the admin onboarding email as soon as Alex confirms peering id or IaC approach.
- Keys: we will generate a 7-day ephemeral key pair and send instructions for rotation. If you want daily rotation, please confirm by EOD Nov 7.
- Peering: we’re holding Nov 11 02:00–04:00 PST as the primary window; please confirm by Nov 9. If that does not work, we’ll fallback to Nov 12 22:00–00:00 PST.
- Procurement: Grace will share a short SOW and trial billing summary; Samir, please let procurement know to expect an email from finance@redwood.ai.

Small acceptance criteria reminder for the MAP kickoff on Nov 15:
- Successful API token fetch as admin (smoke test)
- 100ms median token latency in a 1k sample test (we will supply test harness)
- Validated IP allowlist + successful peering route exchange

Samir — if you confirm Nov 11 window and Alex creates the peering request, we’ll turn on a live monitoring dashboard for the POC and share access.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
VP, Technical Customer Success
Redwood Inference
